tracks.useful_outcome: Independent reruns of self-assessed records, so their stages can count (spec §12.4).

tasks.question: Does an assessor who doesn't maintain the project reproduce the grades of a self-assessed record (applied-butterfly-mult, integer-mult-bounds or the hub)?
methods: rerun the assess playbook at the record's assessed_commit, on a different account
compare grade by grade and name each disagreement
tasks.acceptance_gate: A new record with self_assessed false, the commit and probe model used, and each grade marked agree or disagree with the original, with evidence.
tasks.bottleneck_link: Every recorded stage is self-assessed and counts only after an independent rerun agrees.

tasks.question: Does an independent orientation probe on the same commit give the same answers?
methods: rerun the probe at the recorded commit
tasks.acceptance_gate: A comparison naming each disagreement, with the commit and model used.

first_step.expected: a line starting with discover (the version)

tasks.bottleneck_link: Probe reliability is an open question the grades depend on.

tracks.useful_outcome: Spec changes justified by assessment evidence.

tasks.question: Are the duplicate-rate and response-time thresholds in §3.2 sensible?
methods: measure listed projects in a 14-day window
tasks.acceptance_gate: A proposed change to §3.2 backed by measurements from at least two projects.

first_step.expected: a line starting with discover (the version)

tasks.question: Which gaps found in testing should change the spec, and how: review counted by first response where merging is only intake; duplicate-rate sampling at thousands of PRs; the coordination probe when nothing is open; verification capped by the run policy; hardware-specific help; a missing LICENSE; Stage 1 on very low review capacity?
starting_points: each record's 'Doesn't fit the rubric' section in assessments/
methods: one gap per proposal, with the records that show it
a spec diff and the grade it would change
tasks.acceptance_gate: A spec PR for one gap, citing the assessment records that motivate it and the grades it would change.
tasks.bottleneck_link: The rubric is uncalibrated; these are the gaps real assessments hit.

tracks.useful_outcome: Assessment cheap and repeatable enough to run weekly.

tasks.question: Can the orientation probe run as one command with a pinned model, budget and transcript?
tasks.acceptance_gate: A command that runs the probe against a repo at a pinned commit and saves answers and transcript; tests pass.
tasks.bottleneck_link: Without tooling every assessment is hand work.

tasks.question: Can discover board and discover post read and write protocol messages on GitHub issues, so projects whose transport is issues (the hub itself) get the same claim and handoff state as Discussions?
methods: read issue comments as posts, with the same discover blocks
a test with fixtures for both transports
tasks.acceptance_gate: board and post work on an issues-transport project, with tests; the hub's own board shows its claims.
tasks.bottleneck_link: The hub coordinates through issues, but the board only reads Discussions, which caps its Coordination grade.

tracks.useful_outcome: A listed project of a shape not yet assessed: replication, or conjecture-style.

tasks.question: Does the §3 rubric grade a replication or conjecture-style project sensibly? (A benchmark project, applied-butterfly-mult, is done.)
methods: read-only local assessment of a public candidate repo
tasks.acceptance_gate: A written assessment with per-property grades, evidence links, and every place the rubric didn't fit, kept local and submitted to this repo only.

first_step.expected: a line starting with discover (the version)

tasks.bottleneck_link: The frontier's main gap is projects of other shapes.
allowed_variations: any project shape except a single scalar bound
scope_change_triggers: the candidate's maintainers would need to be contacted
the rubric can't be applied at all

tracks.useful_outcome: Listings that help people choose on human terms.

tasks.question: Which listing signals help a non-expert choose a project without becoming a popularity ranking?
tasks.acceptance_gate: A site change showing the chosen signals, with a note on why each helps choosing.
tasks.bottleneck_link: People choose projects; the gallery is the main surface.
